html:
The Anglo-Egyptian Sudan was the joint rule of Britain and Egypt over Sudan from 1899 to 1956, in practice a British colony. The map shows it in 1914.

It followed the defeat of the Mahdist state. At the Battle of Omdurman in 1898, Kitchener's army of British and Egyptian troops, with machine guns, killed some ten thousand Mahdist fighters. A few weeks later a French force at Fashoda on the upper Nile had to back down. In 1899 Britain and Egypt agreed to share sovereignty, with a British governor-general in Khartoum.

The British built railways and, from 1925, the Gezira Scheme, which irrigated a huge plain between the Blue and White Niles for cotton. They ruled the Muslim north and the mostly non-Muslim south almost as separate countries. Sudan became independent on 1 January 1956, but the north and south were already at war in the First Sudanese Civil War.
sum: The Anglo-Egyptian Sudan was the joint rule of Britain and Egypt over Sudan from 1899 to 1956, in practice a British colony. The map shows it in 1914.
